spec.description: GeoLife, 182 people logging their GPS in Beijing from 2007 to 2012, explored the way Anita Graser does: DuckDB reads and cleans 24.9 million fixes into 50,000 trips, then speeds and stops, flows generalized after Andrienko & Andrienko, and any trip up close.

options.content:
### About the data and the method
**Data.** [GeoLife GPS Trajectories 1.3](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=52367), Microsoft Research Asia: 182 users, April 2007 to August 2012, 24.9 million fixes, mostly in Beijing; 69 users labelled spans of their trips with how they travelled. Released for **non-commercial research** under the Microsoft Research License Agreement. Please cite: Yu Zheng, Lizhu Zhang, Xing Xie, Wei-Ying Ma. *Mining interesting locations and travel sequences from GPS trajectories*, WWW 2009; Yu Zheng, Quannan Li, Yukun Chen, Xing Xie, Wei-Ying Ma. *Understanding Mobility Based on GPS Data*, UbiComp 2008; Yu Zheng, Xing Xie, Wei-Ying Ma. *GeoLife: A Collaborative Social Networking Service among User, location and trajectory*, IEEE Data Engineering Bulletin 2010.

**Where it lives.** The dataset is not in git and not served to browsers. `datasets/geolife/build.sh` downloads it once per instance and runs `build.sql` with DuckDB 1.5.4 (about three minutes); the gateway serves the resulting Parquet to Grafana's DuckDB only, and each tab's figures are computed from it, on the server for the datasets and in the browser (Chaski) for the panels.

**Method.** After Anita Graser's [Movement data in GIS](https://anitagraser.com/movement-data-in-gis/) series:
- *Reading* — [Wrangling hundreds of GPS files with DuckDB, QGIS & Trajectools](https://anitagraser.com/2025/10/12/geolife-gps-track-collection-processing-with-duckdb-qgis-trajectools/) (2025): all the `.plt` files in one DuckDB `read_csv`, the folder as the user, the file as the trajectory.
- *Cleaning* — [Trajectools tutorial: trajectory preprocessing](https://anitagraser.com/2024/09/21/trajectools-tutorial-trajectory-preprocessing/) (2024): one fix per user and second; trips split at 5-minute gaps and at jumps over 300 km/h for over 500 m; a fix that jumps away and back at over 100 km/h removed; trips under 10 fixes, a minute or 100 m dropped. Speed over five fixes. Times are UTC in the data; Beijing time is UTC+8.
- *Stops* — after MovingPandas' stop detection ([2021](https://anitagraser.com/2021/03/28/movement-data-in-gis-35-stop-detection-analysis-with-movingpandas/)): five minutes within 100 m; plus pauses, where the GPS went silent and the next trip starts within 200 m.
- *Flows* — [Visualizing massive trajectory datasets](https://anitagraser.com/2016/11/07/movement-data-in-gis-3-visualizing-massive-trajectory-datasets/) (2016), after G. Andrienko & N. Andrienko, *Spatial generalization and aggregation of massive movement data*, IEEE TVCG 17(2), 2011. Places from the characteristic points grouped on a square grid (no Voronoi step, as in Anita's version), moves counted between consecutive places.

**Limits.** These are the people of one lab in one city, a decade and a half ago, logging when they chose to: the map shows where *they* went, not how Beijing moves. Labelled modes cover 17 % of trips. A mode in *Speed by mode* and on the maps is the label of the fix; on a trip, the label most of its fixes carry.

### 1 · Cleaning — from GPS files to trips
[GeoLife](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/geolife-gps-trajectory-dataset-user-guide/): 182 people in Beijing, most of them at Microsoft Research Asia, logged their GPS from 2007 to 2012 — **24.9 million fixes in 18,670 files**. Following [Anita Graser's protocol](https://anitagraser.com/movement-data-in-gis/), DuckDB reads every file and cleans them as her [Trajectools tutorial](https://anitagraser.com/2024/09/21/trajectools-tutorial-trajectory-preprocessing/) does: one fix a second, **split at gaps**, **remove speed outliers**, drop what is too short. Then *2 · Speed & stops* analyses what is left, and *3 · Generalized flows* and *4 · One trip up close* show the results.

spec.rawSql:
-- Where every trip starts, coloured by whether it starts and ends in Beijing:
-- most do; the rest are the users' travels, as far as the US and Europe.
SELECT lat0 AS latitude, lon0 AS longitude, CASE WHEN beijing THEN 'Beijing' ELSE 'Elsewhere' END AS "where",
       uid AS person, strftime(t0 + INTERVAL 8 HOUR, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') AS "start (Beijing time)",
       km, minutes, CASE WHEN mode = '' THEN 'not labelled' ELSE mode END AS mode
FROM $trips

spec.description: The first fix of every trip after cleaning. *2 · Speed & stops* and *3 · Generalized flows* keep the trips that start and end in Beijing (lat 39.6–40.3, lon 115.9–116.9).
spec.title: Where the trips start

spec.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 MONTH, t0) AS month, mode, count(*) AS trips FROM $trips GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY month

spec.description: Trips a month, by how the user said they travelled. Most labels come from 2008 and 2009, when most of the logging was done.
spec.title: When they were recorded

spec.rawSql: SELECT bin, fixes FROM $sampling ORDER BY bin

spec.description: Seconds between one fix and the next of the same person, before cleaning. Most loggers wrote every 1 to 5 seconds; the long gaps are where trips are split.
spec.title: How often the GPS spoke

spec.rawSql:
SELECT max(trips) FILTER (step = 1) AS "GPS files",
       max(fixes) FILTER (step = 1) AS "Fixes read",
       round(100.0 * max(fixes) FILTER (step = 5) / max(fixes) FILTER (step = 1), 1) AS "Fixes kept",
       max(trips) FILTER (step = 5) AS "Trips",
       max(trips) FILTER (step = 6) AS "Trips in Beijing",
       (SELECT count(DISTINCT uid) FROM $trips) AS "People",
       (SELECT count(*) FROM $trips WHERE mode <> '') AS "Trips labelled"
FROM $cleaning

spec.description: Kept: the share of fixes read that survive cleaning. Labelled: trips where at least half the fixes fall in a span the user labelled with how they travelled.

spec.rawSql: SELECT step, what, fixes, trips FROM $cleaning ORDER BY step

spec.description: Fixes and trips left after each cleaning step. A file is not a trip: one file can hold a day of trips, so splitting at gaps makes more of them, and dropping the short ones fewer.
spec.title: From GPS files to trips

options.content:
### 3 · Results — generalized flows
Millions of fixes are unreadable as lines; Anita Graser [showed in 2016](https://anitagraser.com/2016/11/07/movement-data-in-gis-3-visualizing-massive-trajectory-datasets/) how [Andrienko & Andrienko's generalization](https://doi.org/10.1109/TVCG.2010.44) turns GeoLife into a map of flows. Here it runs live in DuckDB: the points where trips **start, end, stop or turn** are grouped on a grid of the **place size** picked above, each group's centroid becomes a place, and every move of a trip from one place to the next adds to a link. Links fewer trips than the **fewest trips** picked are left out. Bigger places, fewer and stronger links; arrows show the direction, and the circles each place's total.

spec.rawSql: SELECT lat0, lng0, lat1, lng1, trips, moves, place0 AS "from", place1 AS "to" FROM $flows

spec.description: Each link is drawn from place to place, as thick as the trips that made the move; the circles are the places, sized by the trips through them. Hover a link for its trips and moves (a trip that goes back and forth counts once as a trip, every time as a move).
spec.title: Flows between places · ${mode:text}, ${cell:text} places, ${min_trips} trips or more

spec.rawSql:
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT lat0, lng0 FROM $flows UNION SELECT lat1, lng1 FROM $flows)) AS "Places linked",
       count(*) AS "Links", sum(trips) AS "Trip moves"
FROM $flows

spec.description: Places: those with a link in or out. Trip moves: the trips summed over every link, so a trip through five places counts four times.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT "from" AS "From", "to" AS "To", trips AS "Trips",
       round(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(lat1 - lat0) / 2), 2)
             + cos(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(lat1)) * pow(sin(radians(lng1 - lng0) / 2), 2))), 1) AS "Km apart"
FROM (SELECT place0 AS "from", place1 AS "to", * FROM $flows)
ORDER BY trips DESC LIMIT 100

spec.description: The links most trips made, places named by their distance and direction from Tiananmen. The place with most trips is in Zhongguancun, around Tsinghua, Peking University and Microsoft Research Asia, where most users worked and studied.
spec.title: Busiest links

spec.rawSql: SELECT mode, hour(t0 + INTERVAL 8 HOUR) AS hour, count(*) AS trips FROM $trips WHERE beijing GROUP BY ALL

spec.description: Trips starting at each hour of the day, Beijing time, as a share of each mode’s trips. Commuting peaks at 8 and 18; the subway and cars carry the morning.
spec.title: When they travel

options.content:
### 2 · Analysis — how fast, and where they stop
Every 15 seconds of every trip in Beijing, a speed: the distance over five fixes, two either side, over their time, so one jittery fix does not make a sprint. **Left**, the median speed in each H3 cell: ring roads and expressways light up, the old town stays dark. **Right**, every stop: five minutes within 100 m, or the GPS silent between two trips that end and start in the same place. Pick a **mode** above to see one way of travelling; the charts compare them all.

spec.rawSql:
-- The median speed in each cell, for the mode picked; a cell's colour stops at
-- 80 km/h, faster is the same yellow.
SELECT hex, least(kmh, 80) AS kmh, kmh AS "median km/h", trips, fixes
FROM $speed WHERE mode = $mode

spec.description: Median speed of the fixes in each H3 cell (resolution 9, about 0.1 km²), where at least three trips passed. From dark (standing, walking) to yellow (80 km/h and over).
spec.title: How fast · ${mode:text}

spec.rawSql: SELECT mode, kmh, fixes FROM $speeds ORDER BY mode, kmh

spec.description: Share of each mode’s fixes at each speed, in 2 km/h bins. Walking peaks at 4–5 km/h, cycling near 10; bus, car and subway spread wide because they stop and go.
spec.title: Speed by mode

spec.rawSql:
SELECT kind, least(floor(log2(minutes / 5)), 7)::INTEGER AS bin, count(*) AS stops
FROM $stops WHERE $mode IN ('all', mode) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY bin

spec.description: Stops by how long they lasted, on a doubling scale. Dwells inside a trip are mostly short: traffic lights, bus stops, a shop. Pauses between trips are longer: lunch, a meeting, a night.
spec.title: How long they stop · ${mode:text}

spec.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN sqrt(((median(lon) - 116.3975) * 111320 * cos(radians(39.9087))) * ((median(lon) - 116.3975) * 111320 * cos(radians(39.9087))) + ((median(lat) - 39.9087) * 110574) * ((median(lat) - 39.9087) * 110574)) < 750 THEN 'Tiananmen'
            ELSE printf('%.1f km %s', sqrt(((median(lon) - 116.3975) * 111320 * cos(radians(39.9087))) * ((median(lon) - 116.3975) * 111320 * cos(radians(39.9087))) + ((median(lat) - 39.9087) * 110574) * ((median(lat) - 39.9087) * 110574)) / 1000,
                        ['N', 'NE', 'E', 'SE', 'S', 'SW', 'W', 'NW'][floor(((degrees(atan2(((median(lon) - 116.3975) * 111320 * cos(radians(39.9087))), ((median(lat) - 39.9087) * 110574))) + 382.5) % 360) / 45)::INTEGER + 1]) END AS "Where, from Tiananmen",
       count(*) AS "Stops", count(DISTINCT uid) AS "People",
       count(*) FILTER (kind = 'pause') AS "Pauses",
       round(median(minutes)) AS "Median minutes",
       round(median(lat), 4) AS "Lat", round(median(lon), 4) AS "Lon"
FROM $stops WHERE $mode IN ('all', mode)
GROUP BY cell
ORDER BY count(DISTINCT uid) DESC, count(*) DESC
LIMIT 25

spec.description: H3 cells of resolution 8 (about 0.7 km²) with the most stops, of the most people. Tsinghua, Peking University and Microsoft Research Asia, in Zhongguancun, are where most of the users worked and studied.
spec.title: Where they stop most · ${mode:text}

spec.rawSql:
-- Every stop of the mode picked (a pause belongs to the trip it ends).
SELECT lat AS latitude, lon AS longitude, minutes, kind, uid AS person, strftime(t0 + INTERVAL 8 HOUR, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') AS "from (Beijing time)",
       CASE WHEN mode = '' THEN 'not labelled' ELSE mode END AS mode
FROM $stops WHERE $mode IN ('all', mode)

spec.description: Each dot a stop, coloured by how long it lasted (quantiles). Dwell: five minutes within 100 m inside a trip. Pause: the GPS went silent (often indoors) and the next trip started within 200 m, up to 12 hours later.
spec.title: Where they stop · ${mode:text}

options.content:
### 4 · One trip up close
Pick **a person** — those who labelled how they travelled come first — and then **a trip**: the map flies to it, the route coloured by its smoothed speed, the outliers removed in cleaning as **red rings**, the stops as **white circles**. **Press play** on the map and the trip runs again: the traveller changes from walker to bus, bike, car or subway as its user labelled it, and the line on *Speed along the way* follows the clock.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN trip = try_cast($trip AS INTEGER) THEN '▶ ' ELSE '' END
       || strftime(t0 + INTERVAL 8 HOUR, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') AS "Start",
       CASE WHEN mode = '' THEN '–' ELSE mode END AS "Mode",
       km AS "Km", minutes AS "Min", avg_kmh AS "Avg km/h",
       trip AS trip_id, round((lat0 + lat1) / 2, 4) AS lat, round((lon0 + lon1) / 2, 4) AS lng
FROM $trips WHERE uid = try_cast($user AS INTEGER)
ORDER BY trip = try_cast($trip AS INTEGER) DESC, mode <> '' DESC, t0 DESC

spec.description: Every trip of the person picked, in Beijing time: the one followed (▶), then the labelled ones, newest first. Click one to follow it on the map.
spec.title: Trips of person ${user}

spec.rawSql:
-- One traveller, 'trip', so its card stays pinned whichever trip is followed.
SELECT 'trip' AS traveller, time, lat AS latitude, lon AS longitude, speed, kmh, heading,
       CASE WHEN mode = '' THEN 'not labelled' ELSE mode END AS mode,
       strftime(time + INTERVAL 8 HOUR, '%H:%M:%S') AS "time (Beijing)", round(alt_m) AS "altitude m"
FROM $trip_fixes WHERE flag = 'kept' ORDER BY time

SELECT lat AS latitude, lon AS longitude, strftime(time + INTERVAL 8 HOUR, '%H:%M:%S') AS "time (Beijing)", 'speed outlier' AS removed
FROM $trip_fixes WHERE flag = 'spike'

SELECT lat AS latitude, lon AS longitude, kind, minutes, strftime(t0 + INTERVAL 8 HOUR, '%H:%M') AS "from (Beijing)"
FROM $stops WHERE trip = try_cast($trip AS INTEGER)

spec.description: Press play to run the trip again: the traveller takes the shape of the mode its user labelled (a walker where nobody did), with its speed on its card. The route underneath is coloured by smoothed speed. Red rings: fixes removed as speed outliers. White circles: stops.
spec.title: Trip ${trip}

spec.rawSql:
WITH p AS (
  SELECT uid, count(*) AS trips, count(*) FILTER (mode <> '') AS labelled, sum(km) AS km,
         min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1,
         coalesce(arg_max(trip, km) FILTER (beijing AND mode <> ''), arg_max(trip, km)) AS show
  FROM $trips GROUP BY uid
)
SELECT lpad(p.uid::INTEGER::VARCHAR, 3, '0') AS "Person", p.labelled AS "Labelled", p.trips AS "Trips",
       round(p.km) AS "Km", strftime(p.t0, '%Y') || '–' || strftime(p.t1, '%y') AS "Years",
       p.uid, p.show AS trip_id, round((t.lat0 + t.lat1) / 2, 4) AS lat, round((t.lon0 + t.lon1) / 2, 4) AS lng
FROM p JOIN $trips t ON t.trip = p.show
ORDER BY (p.uid = try_cast($user AS INTEGER)) DESC, p.labelled DESC, p.trips DESC

spec.description: One row per person, most labelled trips first. Click a person to see their trips, opening the longest labelled one in Beijing.
spec.title: People

spec.rawSql: SELECT time, kmh, mode FROM $trip_fixes WHERE flag = 'kept' ORDER BY time
SELECT t0, minutes FROM $stops WHERE trip = try_cast($trip AS INTEGER)
SELECT try_cast(rtrim($t_to, 'Z') AS TIMESTAMP) AS at

spec.description: Smoothed speed of each kept fix, coloured by the mode the user labelled; the shaded spans are stops, the line across the map’s clock while it plays.
spec.title: Speed along the way

spec.rawSql:
SELECT round(max(km), 1) AS "Km", max(minutes) AS "Minutes", max(avg_kmh) AS "Avg km/h", max(p95_kmh) AS "95th pct km/h",
       max(fixes) AS "Fixes",
       (SELECT count(*) FROM $trip_fixes WHERE flag = 'spike') AS "Outliers removed",
       (SELECT count(*) FROM $stops WHERE trip = try_cast($trip AS INTEGER)) AS "Stops"
FROM $trips WHERE trip = try_cast($trip AS INTEGER)

spec.description: Km adds up the straight lines between kept fixes. Stops counts the dwells inside the trip and the pause that ends it, if it is in Beijing.

spec.title: GPS trajectories, cleaned and explored — GeoLife

spec.description: How the users said they travelled, for the maps of tabs 2 and 3. All includes the trips nobody labelled.
spec.label: Travelling by
spec.name: mode
spec.query: All : all,Walking : walk,Cycling : bike,Bus : bus,Car and taxi : car,Subway : subway,Train : train

spec.description: The grid the characteristic points are grouped on, in tab 3: each square with enough of them becomes a place.
spec.label: Place size
spec.name: cell

spec.description: Links made by fewer trips are left off the flow map, in tab 3.
spec.label: Fewest trips on a link
spec.name: min_trips

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: the cleaning, step by step, as build.sql ran it
-- (datasets/geolife in the repo): fixes and trips left after each step.
SELECT step, what, fixes, trips FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/geolife/cleaning.parquet' ORDER BY step

-- Seconds between a user's consecutive fixes, before cleaning, in eight bins.
SELECT bin, fixes FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/geolife/sampling.parquet' ORDER BY bin

-- One row per trip after cleaning, 50,000 of them: who, when (UTC), how far,
-- how fast, how they travelled if they said, where it started and ended.
SELECT trip, uid, t0, t1, fixes, km, minutes, avg_kmh, p95_kmh, coalesce(mode, '') AS mode,
       lat0, lon0, lat1, lon1, beijing
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/geolife/trips.parquet'

-- Beijing in H3 cells of resolution 9 (about 0.1 km2): the median speed of the
-- fixes in each, every 15 s of every trip, for all of them and for each mode
-- the users labelled. A cell needs three trips, so one person's walk is not a
-- street.
SELECT h3_latlng_to_cell_string(lat, lon, 9) AS hex, coalesce(mode, 'all') AS mode,
       count(*) AS fixes, count(DISTINCT trip) AS trips, round(median(kmh), 1) AS kmh
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/geolife/track.parquet'
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((hex), (hex, mode))
HAVING count(DISTINCT trip) >= 3 AND coalesce(mode, 'all') <> ''

-- How fast each mode goes: Beijing's fixes every 15 s, in 2 km/h bins.
SELECT mode, least(floor(kmh / 2) * 2, 150)::INTEGER AS kmh, count(*) AS fixes
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/geolife/track.parquet' GROUP BY ALL

-- Every stop in Beijing: five minutes within 100 m inside a trip (dwell), or
-- the GPS silent between two trips that end and start within 200 m (pause).
-- The H3 cell (resolution 8) is worked out here: the browser's DuckDB has no H3.
SELECT trip, uid, kind, t0, minutes, lat, lon, mode, h3_latlng_to_cell_string(lat, lon, 8) AS cell
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/geolife/stops.parquet' WHERE beijing

-- Generalized flows, after Andrienko & Andrienko (2011) as Anita Graser built
-- them for GeoLife in QGIS (2016), live on the place size picked:
-- 1. characteristic points: where trips start, end, stop or turn over 45 deg;
-- 2. grouped on a grid of the size picked, each group's centroid a place;
-- 3. every trip, fix by fix (every 15 s), from place to place: consecutive
--    fixes in one place are one visit, and a move is two visits in a row;
-- 4. a link is every move from one place to another, if enough trips made it.
WITH t AS (
  SELECT trip, t, lat, lon, x, y, keypoint, floor(x / ${cell:raw})::INTEGER AS gx, floor(y / ${cell:raw})::INTEGER AS gy
  FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/geolife/track.parquet'
  WHERE ${mode:sqlstring} IN ('all', mode)
),
places AS (
  SELECT gx, gy, avg(lat) AS lat, avg(lon) AS lon, avg(x) AS x, avg(y) AS y, count(*) AS points
  FROM t WHERE keypoint GROUP BY gx, gy HAVING count(*) >= 3
),
seq AS (
  SELECT trip, gx, gy, lag(gx) OVER w AS px, lag(gy) OVER w AS py
  FROM t SEMI JOIN places USING (gx, gy)
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY trip ORDER BY t)
),
moves AS (
  SELECT px, py, gx, gy, count(*) AS moves, count(DISTINCT trip) AS trips
  FROM seq WHERE px IS NOT NULL AND (gx <> px OR gy <> py)
  GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(DISTINCT trip) >= ${min_trips:raw}
)
SELECT a.lat AS lat0, a.lon AS lng0, b.lat AS lat1, b.lon AS lng1, m.trips, m.moves,
       CASE WHEN sqrt(a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y) < 750 THEN 'Tiananmen'
            ELSE printf('%.1f km %s', sqrt(a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y) / 1000,
                        ['N', 'NE', 'E', 'SE', 'S', 'SW', 'W', 'NW'][floor(((degrees(atan2(a.x, a.y)) + 382.5) % 360) / 45)::INTEGER + 1]) END AS place0,
       CASE WHEN sqrt(b.x * b.x + b.y * b.y) < 750 THEN 'Tiananmen'
            ELSE printf('%.1f km %s', sqrt(b.x * b.x + b.y * b.y) / 1000,
                        ['N', 'NE', 'E', 'SE', 'S', 'SW', 'W', 'NW'][floor(((degrees(atan2(b.x, b.y)) + 382.5) % 360) / 45)::INTEGER + 1]) END AS place1,
       a.points AS points0, b.points AS points1
FROM moves m
JOIN places a ON a.gx = m.px AND a.gy = m.py
JOIN places b ON b.gx = m.gx AND b.gy = m.gy

-- The trip followed, every fix, kept or removed as a speed outlier. Sorted by
-- trip, the file gives it up in one row group.
SELECT t AS time, lat, lon, kmh, least(kmh, 120) AS speed, heading, coalesce(mode, '') AS mode, flag, alt_m
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/geolife/fixes.parquet'
WHERE trip = try_cast(${trip:sqlstring} AS INTEGER)
ORDER BY t
